fixes: Shared supersampled textures for authored tree layers, themed barricades and fixed tank components. Turret/recoil transforms and moving tread strips remain separate.
Native weighted A* with per-request mine filtering and crowd costs; shared prefix costs for route simplification and conservative wall/traffic culling.
Shell, mine and tread-mark artwork rebuilds at most once per displayed frame during physics catch-up. Simulation and sampling cadence are unchanged.
Lazy ricochet candidate enumeration, reused single reflections and cached conservative full-world shot-safety geometry invalidated with cover/navigation rebuilds.

method.runs: Forest 3: two fresh processes per variant and crew size, in before/final/final/before order; four other encounters: one fresh run per variant.
method.baseline: Already includes the prior redraw and retained-vector-component fixes. All current changes are compared against a fresh snapshot from the start of this task.
method.fixture: Real driving/aiming/firing, level-III player weapons, extra enemy test armor; stable cover, normal real-time physics catch-up. Enemy roster unchanged per paired case.

atlas.lifetime: Shared pages load on demand and release after the last registered CanvasItem leaves its scene tree. Cache-release assertion passed.
atlas.editing: Godot editor uses original procedural artwork. New radius/size/style/variation/color variants fall back to that artwork; rebake is optional for performance.
atlas.export: The macOS preset explicitly includes assets/generated/scenery/*.json. PNG resources are included automatically.

seeded_planning_checks.reference_origin: Recorded using the unchanged pre-optimization planners in before-project, seed 72391. Shots match original availability/selection; routes match original minimum grid costs and preserve wall/mine clearance. Native A* may choose different equal-cost waypoints.

validation.editing_fixture: All 50 saved layouts are compared to their authored scenes. The separate add/move/delete exercise clears walls only in a temporary scene instance, preserving the user-edited Mission 1.

limitations: These are short uncapped stress fixtures, not promised game FPS. Four non-Forest-3 comparisons have one repeat per variant.
Normal scheduling permits small differences in battle paths, bullet counts and camera tracking; cover hashes and initial rosters are held constant.

Texture memory rises by roughly 205 MiB and scene creation rises from roughly 0.29 to 0.42 seconds in these fixtures. PNG artwork uses minor antialiasing/rasterization differences, not pixel identity.
GPU timestamp values remain unavailable. CPU/render timing supports reduced submission overhead but does not measure GPU execution time.
Some late bank-shot searches still take about 9 ms individually in the instrumented fixture. Occasional frames remain above the 16.7 ms 60 Hz budget; locked 120/240 FPS is not claimed.
Detailed script-timing wrappers add overhead. Their absolute frame times must not be mixed with the uninstrumented real-time table.
Some smoke tests print ObjectDB/resource teardown diagnostics after PASS. Logs retain these; passing assertions are not a claim that every test is warning-free.
The experimental DDA wall index measured slightly slower and was discarded. Its results are excluded from the accepted comparisons.
